title: Longest String Without Triple Letters
statement:
You have a copies of the letter 'a', b copies of 'b' and c copies of 'c'. Build the longest string you can from them (you do not have to use them all) such that no letter appears three times in a row.

Return any longest such string. Several strings usually qualify, and any of them is accepted. If no letter can be placed, return the empty string.

examples.why: The a and the b split the c's into three groups of at most 2: 2 + 2 + 2 c's plus 2 separators = 8 letters, every letter used.
With nothing to separate them, at most two b's fit.
One b allows two groups of a's, so one a is left over. Placing the b first ("baa") wastes room.

hints: The letter with the most copies is the one at risk of being stranded. Which letter should you place next?
Place the letter with the most copies left, unless the last two characters are already that letter.
If it is blocked, place the letter with the second most copies instead, then return to the first. Stop when neither choice is possible.

explain.intuition:
The danger is running out of separators for the most common letter. So always spend the letter you have most of: that keeps the counts as even as possible and saves the rare letters for when they are needed as separators.

The only time the most common letter cannot go next is when the last two characters are already that letter. Then put down one copy of the next most common letter, which unblocks it. If that letter is gone too, nothing more can be added, and the string is as long as it can get.
steps: Keep the three (count, letter) pairs and an empty result.
Each round, sort the pairs by count, largest first.
Take the first pair with a positive count whose letter would not make three in a row at the end of the result. Append it and decrement its count.
If no pair qualifies, stop and return the result.
pitfalls: Writing two copies of the top letter at once every time. With a = 3, b = 3 that gives aabbaabb… patterns that can strand letters; one letter per step with the 'last two' check is simpler and safe.
Spending a rare letter early. In a = 5, b = 1, starting with b gives only "baa".
Stopping as soon as the top letter is blocked instead of trying the second one.

solutions.title: Search every string
solutions.idea: Try every next letter recursively with memoisation on (counts, last letter, run length) and keep the longest result.

solutions.title: Greedy: most copies first
solutions.idea: Each step place the letter with the most copies left unless that would make three in a row; then take the next one.

followups: Allow at most k equal letters in a row instead of 2. What changes?
Generalise to 26 letters. How does a max-heap replace the sort?
